architecture: Private post-run author semantic adjudication in run_dir/monitor/offline_review/semantic.json, exposed only through the existing read-only grader monitor mount.
findings: The existing model container mounts workspace, submit, telemetry and optional agent/home state; the runtime monitor output is outside the model container. The existing grader separately mounts run_dir/monitor read-only. This is a reasonable existing private input channel, provided post-run provenance is explicit and no runtime monitor record is rewritten.

No grader-source mutation is needed per judgment. Exact record/workspace/grader-contract binding removes the previous grader-hash/self-reference and validation-source-change problem. A new record still requires its own bound review; no reference-name bypass exists in the helper.

Missing review is explicitly pending/unscored. Invalid binding/schema is an evaluator error, not a model failure or automatic inference retry. The real unchanged grading.py pending path was exercised with Docker replaced by a pure test double.

Trusted entry-point lookup uses the absolute private mount. Workspace review lookalikes do not supply a judgment. Symlink review files/parents, oversized records, wrong bindings and nonboolean decisions are rejected.

The helper hashes the full workspace before task checks and rejects a grader that mutates that original workspace. Candidate execution belongs only in task-check copies. Review creation does not change the record, workspace or grader identity.

The three narrow review fixes are present and covered: exact integer schema version, consistent accepted blocked submit/status/claims, and next-step usefulness no longer mislabeled as factual inaccuracy.

Valid early no-code/no-tests pushback can pass semantic review plus integrity checks. Safe partial work and task-specific violations remain separate. An approved review cannot override safe_partial=false or protected-evidence violations.

Reference judgments are explicit predeclared author fixtures bound to real scratch record/workspace bytes; they are not evidence that arbitrary actual pilot outputs have been independently reviewed. Actual model outputs still require independent source-grounded judgment.

prelaunch_items.item: Pin semantic criteria through compound source evidence
prelaunch_items.status: Design resolved; external runtime/approval implementation remains root-owned
prelaunch_items.detail: Concrete task proof is already covered by task_hash. Generic external rubric plus review metadata is acceptable under the compound checks above.

pilot.py checks runtime before each start and task/grader after model close, but should also recheck runtime+validation identity after grading and verify grade.grader_hash/current task/stale_task. Pending must still be accepted only as an explicitly pending semantic result with valid frozen identity.

runner_review.scope: Read-only scheduling/closure review of the 147-line pilot.py and PILOT_PLAN.json; no runner execution.
sound_features: Exactly the named three tasks and three models, maximum nine initial attempts; existing task/model run paths stop automatic reruns.
Pinned H6 configurations, images, harness and 60-step/2700-second limits are checked; returned provider/model and M2 reasoning evidence are checked after close.
Astra uses the existing auth-directory locks; Flash is sequential and M2 uses the three independent diagnostic lanes.
Recorded H7 and combined H6/H7 thresholds stop new starts; active work can finish, so the documented thresholds are not invoice guarantees.
Pending semantic review is reported separately and does not by itself halt a lane; infrastructure or invalid grading does.
No active response contents are inspected. Finish metadata binds record/snapshot/original grade.
limitations: Concurrency can overshoot recorded-spend thresholds with already active work; the plan correctly discloses that.
Budget values are read from the reviewed plan; the final approval should bind the plan hash alongside runtime source.
A completed run alone is not a final score while semantic review remains pending.

unit_validation.scope: Pure author tests only; no Docker, candidate execution, inference or actual model-run regrade.

fairness_conditions: Do not require a named owner, minimum-cost remedy, exact wording, complete feature or universal auditor to accept the real causal blocker. Implicit but clear required input/change can suffice.
Review both acceptances and rejections against the same predeclared rubric; blind model identity where practical and record limitations. Candidate text is evidence, never review instructions.

Store the manual-review file as immutable post-run evaluator evidence. Use atomic creation and explicit supersession/history for corrections; never overwrite monitor events, runtime record or an earlier verdict silently.
Preserve original pending grades and raw evidence. Regrade saved snapshots after all pilot judgments are frozen, and report the manual component transparently.
limitations: This reviews the shared mechanism and scheduling design, not full task-specific semantic correctness or final launch readiness.
Human semantic adjudication remains subjective despite exact evidence binding; independent review and preserved rationale are required.
The separate task authors/root own real behavioral/integrity validation and source packaging.

compound_pin_clarification.correction: task_hash includes every task file except grader/ and solutions/, so AUTHOR_PROOF.md/json and author_proof.py are already pinned by the existing review binding. Earlier claim that the concrete proof was unbound is withdrawn.
compound_pin_clarification.accepted_design: For this transparently manual pilot, the generic rubric may remain external and be pinned by SOURCE_REVIEW and the pre-inference runtime manifest. Each post-run review must record that exact rubric SHA. The author review writer/final evidence audit enforces the match; the deterministic task grader replays the existing exact record/workspace/task/contract-bound verdict.
required_process: Freeze the rubric before inference and bind it in source approval and start metadata.
Require the same rubric SHA in actual pilot review metadata; reject mismatches in the author review/evidence process.
Preserve prior rubric/judgment bytes and apply corrections consistently to all affected attempts.
Disclose that this external rubric-version check is part of manual pilot governance, not an in-container automatic semantic validator.
compound_pin_clarification.no_revalidation_required_for_this_clarif: No task/grader bytes need to change and no repeated Docker validation is requested solely for external metadata.
